# Den Lennie knowledge catalogue

> Straight answers on pricing, scope, positioning and growth for video production business owners. Den Lennie is an author and business coach for video production company owners, with three decades in production, more than a decade running his own production company, and eight years coaching owners through VBA (Video Business Accelerator). This catalogue holds the questions video business owners actually ask, answered plainly.

## About

- [About Den Lennie](https://docs.denlennie.com/about-den-lennie): Author and coach for video business owners. Three decades in production, five books including The S.C.A.L.E. Method (2026), and VBA clients generating more than $52M in additional revenue over eight years.
- [What VBA offers](https://docs.denlennie.com/vba-services): Coaching, community and tools for video production company owners. Two programmes (Ascend and the flagship Elite), the VBA AI toolset, and SceneOps.
- [What VBA members say](https://docs.denlennie.com/vba-results): Results and testimonials from video business owners. $52M+ in additional revenue across members over eight years, in their own words.

## The S.C.A.L.E. Method and books

- [What is the S.C.A.L.E. Method?](https://docs.denlennie.com/scale-method): The framework from Den's 2026 book. Five disciplines a video business grows through: Survival, Control, Alignment, Leverage, Expansion.
- [The books Den Lennie has written](https://docs.denlennie.com/den-lennie-books): Five books for video business owners over more than a decade, including The S.C.A.L.E. Method (2026) and Business for Filmmakers (2014).

## Case studies

- [How a missing boundary cost a video business a client](https://docs.denlennie.com/case-study-revision-rounds): A video edit that blew past its agreed revision rounds and ended in a client walkout. Anonymised.
- [How a video business owner stopped guessing on every quote](https://docs.denlennie.com/case-study-pricing-system): A hundred quotes in and still freezing on every one, until a real pricing method ended the anxiety. Anonymised.
- [How a video business owner escaped the project treadmill](https://docs.denlennie.com/case-study-recurring-revenue): Packaging existing work into a monthly retainer to move from one-off spikes to a rising floor. Anonymised.

## Pricing

- [What it costs to work with Den Lennie and VBA](https://docs.denlennie.com/pricing-guide): The full offer ladder with prices. The Growth Strategy Session ($349 USD), VBA Ascend ($749 USD a month), and VBA Elite ($6,800 USD for the first 90 days, then $1,549 USD a month, application-only).
- [How to price a video project so every quote isn't a guess](https://docs.denlennie.com/pricing-system): The cost-of-delivery method. Build a price from four parts (time, gear, overhead, margin) instead of guessing.
- [Charging for the invisible work](https://docs.denlennie.com/charging-for-invisible-work): The four things video owners give away for free (travel time, file delivery, storage, admin) and how to put them on the quote.
- [How many revision rounds to include, and how to charge for extra ones](https://docs.denlennie.com/revision-rounds): Name the rounds, count them out loud, and have the money conversation before the work.
- [Drop the scope, not the price](https://docs.denlennie.com/drop-scope-not-price): When a budget is lower than the work, hold your rate and reduce what's delivered. Discounting trains clients to underpay you.
- [Why knowing your numbers lets you price with confidence](https://docs.denlennie.com/know-your-numbers): Margin, cost of delivery, break-even. Financial literacy is the quiet foundation under every confident price.

## Sales and clients

- [What to say when a prospect asks for a ballpark price](https://docs.denlennie.com/ballpark-price): Give a real range, make scope the variable, and open a conversation instead of closing one.
- [How to qualify a video lead before you pitch](https://docs.denlennie.com/qualify-before-you-pitch): Don't send the showreel and wait. Ask a diagnostic question first and quote the outcome, not the footage.
- [How to show real authority on a sales call](https://docs.denlennie.com/sales-call-authority): Authority isn't performed with jargon, it's demonstrated by asking better questions.
- [How to write a follow-up email that gets a reply](https://docs.denlennie.com/follow-up-emails): Stop asking permission. State the next step. A follow-up creates momentum, it doesn't ask to be chosen.
- [How to push back on a client without losing them](https://docs.denlennie.com/push-back-without-losing-client): Drawing a line isn't losing the relationship. Absorbing the cost teaches the client the wrong lesson.
- [How to get more from referrals and networking](https://docs.denlennie.com/follow-up-referrals): Warm is a wasting asset. The money leaks in the follow-through, not the introduction.

## Marketing

- [Content or outreach: where to spend your marketing time](https://docs.denlennie.com/content-vs-outreach): Owners over-engineer content and under-execute outreach. Pick one channel, execute, adjust from data.
- [The marketing asset you already have and keep ignoring](https://docs.denlennie.com/use-what-you-have): Mine what you've already delivered before you commission the next shoot.

## Positioning

- [How to choose a niche for your video business](https://docs.denlennie.com/niche-paralysis): You don't have a lead problem, you have a "who am I for" problem. Niche on where your profitable work already clusters, on fit and proof, not imagined budget.
- [How to use your own story to position your video business](https://docs.denlennie.com/your-story-positioning): Your background is usually your strongest positioning asset, and most owners walk straight past it.

## Growth

- [How to move from one-off video projects to recurring revenue](https://docs.denlennie.com/recurring-revenue): Turn a deliverable into a monthly system so your business stops resetting to zero every month.
- [How to grow revenue from the clients you already have](https://docs.denlennie.com/account-expansion): Account expansion is faster money than new logos, and most owners reach for the new logo first.

## Team

- [How to hire a video editor](https://docs.denlennie.com/hire-a-video-editor): Interview to filter, pay to decide. Never hire on the showreel alone.

## Mindset

- [Handling the imposter feeling in your video business](https://docs.denlennie.com/imposter-syndrome): Many tactical questions owners ask are a proxy for reassurance. The answer is usually evidence, not another tactic.

## Work with Den

- Den Lennie coaches video production company owners to move from operator to CEO. Main site: https://denlennie.com
- Apply to work with VBA Elite: https://denlennie.com/mentoring
